intro: Hi! Today you'll learn the words people use in the news, at university and in meetings to talk about science and research, climate change and energy, and social issues like unemployment and inequality. You'll also learn how to talk about difficult topics in a calm, balanced way. Warm-up: what's one problem in your city that people often discuss?
teachingNotes: Teach the words in small themed groups with an Indonesian gloss and practise them in sentences at B2, not only as translations. Science and research: research (riset, penelitian), a study / studies (sebuah penelitian), an experiment (eksperimen, percobaan), data (data), evidence (bukti), findings (temuan, hasil penelitian), a breakthrough (terobosan), innovation (inovasi), develop (mengembangkan), discover (menemukan sesuatu yang sudah ada) vs invent (menciptakan sesuatu yang baru). Collocations: do / conduct / carry out research or an experiment, research on / into something, the findings show that…, make a breakthrough.

The node's second common error is *'There are many researches about it' → There is a lot of research on it. research and evidence are uncountable (tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu): no -s, no a, use a lot of / much / some research, a piece of evidence. To count, use study: two studies, many studies. data: traditionally plural (the data show), but today 'the data shows' is also very common: accept both, never 'datas'. Indonesian has no plural marking, so 'riset-riset' and 'banyak bukti' push learners to 'researches' and 'evidences'. menemukan = discover AND invent: Fleming discovered penicillin (it already existed in nature); the telephone was invented (it didn't exist before).

Climate and energy. The learner met climate change, global warming, pollution, reduce/reuse/recycle and save energy in b1-vocab-environment-travel: recap in a line, don't reteach. New: emissions (emisi; usually plural: carbon emissions, reduce emissions), greenhouse gases (gas rumah kaca), fossil fuels (bahan bakar fosil: coal, oil, gas), renewable energy (energi terbarukan: solar, wind, geothermal, hydro), carbon footprint (jejak karbon), sustainable (berkelanjutan), switch to (beralih ke). The node's first common error: *'The climate change is a big problem' → Climate change is a big problem (no the: it's a general topic, like pollution or education). Third common error: *'Pollution makes the environment broken' → Pollution damages / harms / pollutes the environment. broken (rusak) is for things like a phone or a chair; for nature, health and the economy use damage or harm.

Social issues: inequality (ketimpangan, kesenjangan), unemployment (pengangguran), access to education / healthcare (akses ke pendidikan / layanan kesehatan; access TO, not 'access of'), urbanisation (urbanisasi; American urbanization), an ageing population (populasi yang menua; American aging), poverty (kemiskinan). Neutral, balanced language: Some people argue that … ; Others believe … ; On the other hand, … ; It could be argued that … (a phrase to remember: don't teach the grammar behind it); may / might / can to avoid saying something is always true. Avoid loaded words (destroy, lazy, terrible, everyone knows) and don't take a side in political questions; if the learner asks your opinion on politics, give both sides.

Facts: keep them general and true, without statistics, rankings or dates. Safe facts: Indonesia has many volcanoes and a lot of geothermal potential; coal is still a big source of electricity in Indonesia; Japan and South Korea have ageing populations while Indonesia's population is relatively young; many people move from villages to big cities. Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 (well known).

Limits: A0–B1 grammar only (all tenses up to present perfect continuous and past perfect, first and second conditionals, modals, present and past simple passive, reported statements, defining relative clauses, gerunds and infinitives). No third conditional, wish, past modals (must have…), participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses or advanced passive. Don't test near-synonyms against each other: research/study as a general idea, damage/harm/pollute, think/believe/argue, conduct/do/carry out, results/findings.

keyPoints.title: Science, research and innovation
keyPoints.explanation: research (riset) and evidence (bukti) are uncountable: a lot of research, some evidence, never 'many researches' or 'evidences'. To count, use study: two studies. data: the data show / the data shows (both used), never 'datas'. You do, conduct or carry out research or an experiment; research on / into a topic; the findings (hasil penelitian) show that…; make a breakthrough (terobosan); develop a vaccine; innovation (inovasi). menemukan has two English words: discover (it already existed) and invent (it's new).

examples.en: There is a lot of research on rice that needs less water.
examples.id: Ada banyak riset tentang padi yang butuh lebih sedikit air.

examples.en: The findings show that people who sleep less make more mistakes at work.
examples.id: Hasil penelitiannya menunjukkan bahwa orang yang kurang tidur membuat lebih banyak kesalahan di tempat kerja.
Alexander Fleming menemukan penisilin pada tahun 1928.

id.title: Sains, riset dan inovasi
id.explanation: research (riset) dan evidence (bukti) tidak bisa dihitung (uncountable): a lot of research, some evidence, tidak pernah 'many researches' atau 'evidences'. Kalau mau menghitung, pakai study: two studies (dua penelitian). data: the data show / the data shows (dua-duanya dipakai), tidak pernah 'datas'. Kamu do, conduct atau carry out research atau an experiment (melakukan riset/eksperimen); research on / into sebuah topik; the findings (hasil penelitian) show that…; make a breakthrough (membuat terobosan); develop a vaccine (mengembangkan vaksin); innovation (inovasi). menemukan punya dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris: discover (sudah ada sebelumnya) dan invent (benar-benar baru).

keyPoints.title: Climate change and energy
keyPoints.explanation: Climate change has no the: Climate change is a big problem (not 'The climate change'). Cars, factories and power stations produce emissions (carbon emissions) and greenhouse gases. Fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) run out; renewable energy (solar, wind, geothermal, hydro) doesn't. Your carbon footprint is how much CO2 your life produces. Sustainable = it can continue without hurting the planet. Pollution damages / harms the environment: never 'makes the environment broken'.

examples.en: Climate change is making heavy rain more common in many places.
examples.id: Perubahan iklim membuat hujan deras makin sering di banyak tempat.

examples.en: Indonesia has many volcanoes, so it has a lot of geothermal energy.
examples.id: Indonesia punya banyak gunung berapi, jadi punya banyak energi panas bumi.

examples.en: Plastic waste damages the ocean and harms sea animals.
examples.id: Sampah plastik merusak laut dan membahayakan hewan laut.

id.title: Perubahan iklim dan energi
id.explanation: Climate change tidak pakai the: Climate change is a big problem (bukan 'The climate change'). Mobil, pabrik dan pembangkit listrik menghasilkan emissions (emisi karbon) dan greenhouse gases (gas rumah kaca). Fossil fuels (bahan bakar fosil: batu bara, minyak, gas) bisa habis; renewable energy (energi terbarukan: surya, angin, panas bumi, air) tidak. Carbon footprint (jejak karbon) = seberapa banyak CO2 yang dihasilkan gaya hidupmu. Sustainable (berkelanjutan) = bisa terus berjalan tanpa merugikan bumi. Polusi damages / harms (merusak / membahayakan) lingkungan: tidak pernah 'makes the environment broken'.

keyPoints.title: Social issues in neutral, balanced language
keyPoints.explanation: Words: inequality (the gap between rich and poor), unemployment (people who want a job but can't find one), poverty, access to education / healthcare (access TO), urbanisation (people moving to cities; American urbanization), an ageing population (more older people; American aging). To sound balanced, give more than one side: Some people argue that … Others believe … On the other hand, … It could be argued that … (a phrase to remember). Use may / might / can instead of 'always', and avoid loaded words like destroy, lazy or terrible.

examples.en: Some people argue that online classes save time. On the other hand, students in remote villages often have a weak signal.
examples.id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa kelas online menghemat waktu. Di sisi lain, pelajar di desa terpencil sering punya sinyal yang lemah.

examples.en: Japan has an ageing population, so it needs more care workers.
examples.id: Jepang punya populasi yang menua, jadi butuh lebih banyak tenaga perawat.

examples.en: Urbanisation can create jobs, but it may also lead to more traffic and higher rents.
examples.id: Urbanisasi bisa menciptakan lapangan kerja, tapi juga bisa menyebabkan lebih banyak macet dan sewa yang lebih mahal.

id.title: Isu sosial dengan bahasa yang netral dan berimbang
id.explanation: Kata-kata: inequality (ketimpangan: jarak antara kaya dan miskin), unemployment (pengangguran: orang yang mau bekerja tapi tidak dapat pekerjaan), poverty (kemiskinan), access to education / healthcare (akses ke pendidikan / layanan kesehatan; pakai TO), urbanisation (urbanisasi: orang pindah ke kota; Amerika: urbanization), an ageing population (populasi yang menua: makin banyak orang tua; Amerika: aging). Supaya terdengar berimbang, sebutkan lebih dari satu sisi: Some people argue that … (sebagian orang berpendapat …) Others believe … (yang lain percaya …) On the other hand, … (di sisi lain …) It could be argued that … (bisa dikatakan bahwa …, frasa untuk dihafal). Pakai may / might / can daripada 'always', dan hindari kata yang berat sebelah seperti destroy, lazy atau terrible.

'some research' = 90 (grammatical, but loses 'many'). 'many research' (no -s) = 40 (still treats research as countable). 'a lot of researches' = 30. Unchanged ('many researches') = 0.

break through

assessment.rubric: Correct: breakthrough (terobosan; make a breakthrough). 'discovery' = 60 (natural English, but it isn't terobosan and the gloss asks for it). 'innovation' = 40 (you don't 'make a major innovation'). Spelling error that keeps the word clear ('breaktrough') = 80.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one word: The new factory in Karawang created 2,000 jobs, so ___ (the number of people who want to work but can't find a job) in the area went down.

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani is writing a balanced report about online classes. Complete with one word: It could be ___ that online classes help students in remote areas. However, they need a good internet connection.

said
assessment.rubric: Correct: It could be argued that … (a neutral phrase: it shows an idea without saying it's your strong opinion). 'said' is also accepted. 'argue' = 50 (the phrase needs the third form). 'thought' = 60 (understandable but not the fixed phrase). 'true' = 20 (not neutral: it changes the meaning).

material.title: Science and research: research, study, evidence, data

id.title: Sains dan riset: research, study, evidence, data

blocks.text:
These words come up in the news, at university and in meetings:
- **research** (riset, penelitian): *She does research on dengue.* You **do**, **conduct** (more formal) or **carry out** research. Research **on** or **into** a topic.
- **a study** (sebuah penelitian, one piece of research): *A new study shows that…*
- **an experiment** (eksperimen, percobaan): *conduct an experiment*
- **data** (data): the facts and numbers a study collects
- **evidence** (bukti): facts that show something is true
- **findings** (temuan, hasil penelitian): what a study finds. *The findings show that…*
- **a scientist** (ilmuwan) / **a researcher** (peneliti)

The big trap: some of these words are **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu, like *water* or *rice*): no **-s** and no **a**.

id.text:
Kata-kata ini sering muncul di berita, di kampus dan di rapat:
- **research** (riset, penelitian): *She does research on dengue.* Kamu **do**, **conduct** (lebih formal) atau **carry out** research. Research **on** atau **into** sebuah topik.
- **a study** (sebuah penelitian, satu riset): *A new study shows that…*
- **an experiment** (eksperimen, percobaan): *conduct an experiment*
- **data** (data): fakta dan angka yang dikumpulkan sebuah penelitian
- **evidence** (bukti): fakta yang menunjukkan sesuatu itu benar
- **findings** (temuan, hasil penelitian): apa yang ditemukan sebuah penelitian. *The findings show that…*
- **a scientist** (ilmuwan) / **a researcher** (peneliti)

Jebakan utamanya: beberapa kata ini **uncountable** (tidak bisa dihitung satu per satu, seperti *water* atau *rice*): tidak pakai **-s** dan tidak pakai **a**.

rows.en: There is a lot of research on rice that needs less water.
rows.id: Ada banyak riset tentang padi yang butuh lebih sedikit air.
rows.note: a lot of research, not 'many researches'

id.note: a lot of research, bukan 'many researches'

rows.en: Two new studies show that walking every day helps your heart.
rows.id: Dua penelitian baru menunjukkan bahwa berjalan kaki setiap hari baik untuk jantung.
rows.note: study is countable: one study, two studies

id.note: study bisa dihitung: one study, two studies

rows.en: The police found some evidence near the car.
rows.id: Polisi menemukan beberapa bukti di dekat mobil itu.
rows.note: some evidence / a piece of evidence, not 'evidences'

id.note: some evidence / a piece of evidence, bukan 'evidences'

rows.en: The data shows that more people are taking the MRT.
rows.id: Datanya menunjukkan bahwa makin banyak orang naik MRT.
rows.note: the data show is also correct (more formal)

id.note: the data show juga benar (lebih formal)

blocks.text:
**Why not 'many researches'?** Indonesian has no plural marking, and *riset-riset* or *banyak penelitian* feel natural, so learners write *'many researches'* and *'evidences'*. In English, **research** and **evidence** are uncountable: say **a lot of research**, **much research**, **some evidence**, **a piece of evidence**.
Want to count? Use **study**: *one study, three studies*.

**data** is special. In Latin it was the plural of *datum*, so formal and scientific English often says **the data show**. In everyday English **the data shows** is very common too. Both are fine. But never *'datas'*.

id.text:
**Kenapa bukan 'many researches'?** Bahasa Indonesia tidak menandai jamak, dan *riset-riset* atau *banyak penelitian* terasa wajar, jadi orang sering menulis *'many researches'* dan *'evidences'*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **research** dan **evidence** tidak bisa dihitung: bilang **a lot of research**, **much research**, **some evidence**, **a piece of evidence**.
Mau menghitung? Pakai **study**: *one study, three studies*.

**data** itu khusus. Dalam bahasa Latin, data adalah bentuk jamak dari *datum*, jadi bahasa Inggris formal dan ilmiah sering bilang **the data show**. Dalam bahasa sehari-hari, **the data shows** juga sangat umum. Dua-duanya boleh. Tapi tidak pernah *'datas'*.

options: The doctor found no evidences of a virus.
The doctor found no evidence of a virus.
The doctor found no an evidence of a virus.
blocks.explain: evidence is uncountable: no -s and no a. 'no evidence' is the natural phrase. To count it, say 'a piece of evidence'.

id.explain: evidence tidak bisa dihitung: tidak pakai -s dan tidak pakai a. 'no evidence' adalah frasa yang wajar. Kalau mau menghitung, bilang 'a piece of evidence'.

material.title: From idea to breakthrough: develop, discover, invent

id.title: Dari ide sampai terobosan: develop, discover, invent

blocks.text:
Words for new ideas and inventions:
- **innovation** (inovasi): new ideas or new ways of doing things. *Indonesia's startups need innovation.* As a general idea it has no -s; one new product can be *an innovation*.
- **develop** (mengembangkan): *develop a vaccine, develop an app*. The noun is **development**.
- **a breakthrough** (terobosan): a very important new discovery after a lot of work. You **make a breakthrough**.
- **technology** (teknologi), **a scientific discovery** (penemuan ilmiah)

**One Indonesian word, two English words.** *Menemukan* can be:
- **discover** = find something that **already existed** (in nature, in the world): *discover a new species of frog in Papua*
- **invent** = make something **completely new** that didn't exist before: *invent the telephone, invent a new machine*

id.text:
Kata-kata untuk ide baru dan penemuan:
- **innovation** (inovasi): ide baru atau cara baru melakukan sesuatu. *Indonesia's startups need innovation.* Sebagai ide umum tidak pakai -s; satu produk baru bisa disebut *an innovation*.
- **develop** (mengembangkan): *develop a vaccine, develop an app*. Kata bendanya **development**.
- **a breakthrough** (terobosan): penemuan baru yang sangat penting setelah kerja keras yang lama. Kamu **make a breakthrough**.
- **technology** (teknologi), **a scientific discovery** (penemuan ilmiah)

**Satu kata Indonesia, dua kata Inggris.** *Menemukan* bisa berarti:
- **discover** = menemukan sesuatu yang **sudah ada** (di alam, di dunia): *discover a new species of frog in Papua*
- **invent** = menciptakan sesuatu yang **benar-benar baru**, yang belum pernah ada: *invent the telephone, invent a new machine*

rows.note: discover: penicillin comes from a mould that already existed

rows.note: invent: the light bulb didn't exist before

id.note: invent: bola lampu belum pernah ada sebelumnya

rows.en: A startup in Bandung is developing an app for small farmers.
rows.id: Sebuah startup di Bandung sedang mengembangkan aplikasi untuk petani kecil.

rows.en: The researchers made a breakthrough after years of failed experiments.
rows.id: Para peneliti membuat terobosan setelah bertahun-tahun eksperimen yang gagal.

blocks.prompt: Scientists found a new kind of orchid in the forests of Kalimantan. Complete: They ___ a new orchid.
blocks.explain: The orchid already existed in the forest: they found it, so they discovered it. You invent something that didn't exist before (a machine), and you develop a product step by step.

id.prompt: Para ilmuwan menemukan jenis anggrek baru di hutan Kalimantan. Lengkapi: They ___ a new orchid.
id.explain: Anggrek itu sudah ada di hutan: mereka menemukannya, jadi discovered. Invent untuk sesuatu yang belum pernah ada (misalnya mesin), dan develop untuk mengembangkan produk sedikit demi sedikit.

blocks.text:
In B1 you learned **pollution**, **climate change**, **global warming** and **reduce, reuse, recycle**. Now the words from news reports about energy:
- **emissions** (emisi): gases that cars, factories and power stations send into the air. Usually plural: *carbon emissions, reduce emissions*.
- **greenhouse gases** (gas rumah kaca): gases like CO2 that keep heat in the air and make the planet warmer.
- **fossil fuels** (bahan bakar fosil): **coal** (batu bara), **oil** (minyak bumi) and **gas**. They **run out** one day.
- **renewable energy** (energi terbarukan): energy that doesn't run out: **solar** (dari matahari), **wind** (angin), **geothermal** (panas bumi: heat from under the ground) and **hydro** (tenaga air).
- **carbon footprint** (jejak karbon): how much CO2 your lifestyle produces.
- **sustainable** (berkelanjutan): it can continue for a long time without hurting the planet.
- **switch to** (beralih ke): *switch to solar power*

id.text:
Di B1 kamu sudah belajar **pollution**, **climate change**, **global warming** dan **reduce, reuse, recycle**. Sekarang kata-kata dari berita tentang energi:
- **emissions** (emisi): gas yang dikeluarkan mobil, pabrik dan pembangkit listrik ke udara. Biasanya jamak: *carbon emissions, reduce emissions*.
- **greenhouse gases** (gas rumah kaca): gas seperti CO2 yang menahan panas di udara dan membuat bumi makin panas.
- **fossil fuels** (bahan bakar fosil): **coal** (batu bara), **oil** (minyak bumi) dan **gas**. Suatu hari bisa **run out** (habis).
- **renewable energy** (energi terbarukan): energi yang tidak habis: **solar** (dari matahari), **wind** (angin), **geothermal** (panas bumi: panas dari dalam tanah) dan **hydro** (tenaga air).
- **carbon footprint** (jejak karbon): seberapa banyak CO2 yang dihasilkan gaya hidupmu.
- **sustainable** (berkelanjutan): bisa terus berjalan lama tanpa merugikan bumi.
- **switch to** (beralih ke): *switch to solar power*

blocks.text:
**Two traps from Indonesian.**
1. *Perubahan iklim adalah masalah besar* → **Climate change is a big problem.** Not *'The climate change'*. When you talk about a big general topic, English uses no *the*: *Climate change, pollution, education and unemployment are big issues.* (Compare: *the climate in Bandung* = one specific place.)
2. *Polusi membuat lingkungan rusak* → not *'makes the environment broken'*. **broken** (rusak) is for things like a phone, a chair or a leg. For nature, health or the economy, use **damage** or **harm**: **Pollution damages the environment.** **Smoking harms your health.** Or **pollute**: *Factories pollute the river.*

id.text:
**Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia.**
1. *Perubahan iklim adalah masalah besar* → **Climate change is a big problem.** Bukan *'The climate change'*. Kalau membicarakan topik umum yang besar, bahasa Inggris tidak pakai *the*: *Climate change, pollution, education and unemployment are big issues.* (Bandingkan: *the climate in Bandung* = iklim di satu tempat tertentu.)
2. *Polusi membuat lingkungan rusak* → bukan *'makes the environment broken'*. **broken** (rusak) untuk benda seperti HP, kursi atau kaki yang patah. Untuk alam, kesehatan atau ekonomi, pakai **damage** atau **harm**: **Pollution damages the environment.** **Smoking harms your health.** Atau **pollute** (mencemari): *Factories pollute the river.*

blocks.text:
Words for issues people discuss in society (masyarakat):
- **inequality** (ketimpangan, kesenjangan): the gap between rich and poor
- **poverty** (kemiskinan)
- **unemployment** (pengangguran): people want to work but can't find a job. The people are **unemployed**.
- **access to education / healthcare** (akses ke pendidikan / layanan kesehatan). Use **to**: not *'access of'*.
- **urbanisation** (urbanisasi): people moving from villages to cities. American spelling: **urbanization**.
- **an ageing population** (populasi yang menua): more and more older people. American: **aging**.

**How to sound balanced** (berimbang). On difficult topics, show more than one side and don't attack people:
- **Some people argue that …** / **Others believe that …**
- **On the other hand, …** (di sisi lain)
- **It could be argued that …** (bisa dikatakan bahwa …): just learn it as a phrase.
- Use **may, might, can** and **often** instead of *always*: *Urbanisation can create jobs.*

id.text:
Kata-kata untuk isu yang dibahas di masyarakat (society):
- **inequality** (ketimpangan, kesenjangan): jarak antara yang kaya dan yang miskin
- **poverty** (kemiskinan)
- **unemployment** (pengangguran): orang mau bekerja tapi tidak dapat pekerjaan. Orangnya disebut **unemployed**.
- **access to education / healthcare** (akses ke pendidikan / layanan kesehatan). Pakai **to**: bukan *'access of'*.
- **urbanisation** (urbanisasi): orang pindah dari desa ke kota. Ejaan Amerika: **urbanization**.
- **an ageing population** (populasi yang menua): makin banyak orang lanjut usia. Amerika: **aging**.

**Cara terdengar berimbang.** Untuk topik yang sulit, tunjukkan lebih dari satu sisi dan jangan menyerang orang:
- **Some people argue that …** (sebagian orang berpendapat …) / **Others believe that …** (yang lain percaya …)
- **On the other hand, …** (di sisi lain)
- **It could be argued that …** (bisa dikatakan bahwa …): hafalkan saja sebagai frasa.
- Pakai **may, might, can** dan **often** daripada *always*: *Urbanisation can create jobs.*

blocks.text:
**Neutral, not loaded.** Words like *destroy*, *lazy*, *terrible* or *everyone knows* make you sound angry or one-sided. Compare:
- One-sided: *'Social media is destroying young people.'*
- Balanced: **Some people argue that social media can harm young people's sleep. On the other hand, it helps them learn and stay in touch.**

**society, people or the public?** Indonesian *masyarakat* has several English words: **society** (masyarakat as a whole: *problems in society*), **the public** (masyarakat umum: *open to the public*), **people** or **the community** (warga: *the local community*).

id.text:
**Netral, bukan berat sebelah.** Kata seperti *destroy*, *lazy*, *terrible* atau *everyone knows* membuatmu terdengar marah atau memihak. Bandingkan:
- Memihak: *'Social media is destroying young people.'*
- Berimbang: **Some people argue that social media can harm young people's sleep. On the other hand, it helps them learn and stay in touch.**

**society, people atau the public?** Kata *masyarakat* punya beberapa padanan dalam bahasa Inggris: **society** (masyarakat secara keseluruhan: *problems in society*), **the public** (masyarakat umum: *open to the public*), **people** atau **the community** (warga: *the local community*).

blocks.prompt: Sari is writing about motorbike taxis (ojek online) for a university essay. Which sentence is the most balanced?
options: Ojek online drivers are destroying traffic in every city.
Ojek online gives many people work. On the other hand, some drivers say their income is not stable.
Everyone knows ojek online is the best job in Indonesia.
blocks.explain: The second sentence shows two sides (jobs and unstable income) and uses calm words. The first uses the loaded word destroying and 'every city'; the third uses 'Everyone knows' and 'the best', which sound one-sided.

id.prompt: Sari menulis tentang ojek online untuk esai kuliah. Kalimat mana yang paling berimbang?
id.explain: Kalimat kedua menunjukkan dua sisi (lapangan kerja dan penghasilan yang tidak stabil) dengan kata-kata yang tenang. Kalimat pertama memakai kata berat sebelah destroying dan 'every city'; kalimat ketiga memakai 'Everyone knows' dan 'the best', yang terdengar memihak.
